description: Active piezo buzzer, 3-5 V, 30 mA, 80 dB, 2 pins (+/-)
typicalApplication: ACTIVE buzzer: it has its own oscillator, so a steady DC level on + makes it sound -- no tone waveform needed (a PASSIVE buzzer would need one). Pin 1 = +, pin 2 = -. At ~25-30 mA it is above the ~20 mA an AVR/ESP32 GPIO should source, so drive it low-side: GPIO -> 1 kOhm -> NPN base (MMBT3904/2N3904), buzzer + to the 5 V rail and buzzer - to the collector. Mark BZ+/BZ- on the silkscreen.

That is 20+ parts before the user's circuit; for a beginner/hobby prompt choose RaspberryPi_Pico (module with all of this on board) unless the user explicitly asks for a bare RP2040.

description: RGB LED, 5050 PLCC-4, COMMON CATHODE (R/G/B anodes + shared K)
typicalApplication: COMMON-CATHODE RGB LED: pin 2 (K) to GND, pins 1/3/4 are the R/G/B anodes. Each colour needs its OWN series resistor between the driving GPIO and its anode — the channels have different forward voltages (red ~2.0 V, green/blue ~3.0-3.2 V), so ~330 Ohm for red and ~150-220 Ohm for green/blue off a 3.3 V rail. Use PWM-capable pins if you want colour mixing. Never wire a channel straight to a GPIO.

description: Raspberry Pi 40-pin HAT GPIO header, 2x20 2.54mm, BCM pin map
typicalApplication: The board-side view of the Raspberry Pi 40-pin GPIO bank for HAT designs: the header SUPPLIES 3V3/5V/GND to the board, and every GPIO is 3.3 V-only (NOT 5 V-tolerant). GPIO2/GPIO3 are I2C1 with fixed 1.8 kOhm pull-ups on the Pi; GPIO14/15 default to the Linux serial console; ID_SD/ID_SC (pins 27/28) are reserved for the HAT ID EEPROM and must not be used as GPIO. Hardware PWM only on GPIO12/13/18/19. The Pi has no on-chip ADC - use an external ADC (ADS1115/MCP3008) for analog inputs.

description: Arduino Uno R3 shield header set (D0-D13, A0-A5, power), 2.54mm
typicalApplication: The shield-side view of the Arduino Uno R3 header pattern for designing shields: the base board SUPPLIES 5V/3V3/IOREF and GND up through the header (5 V logic - D pins are 5 V). D0/D1 are shared with the Uno's USB-serial console (avoid unless the shield is a serial device); I2C is on A4/A5 (duplicated on the SDA/SCL pins); SPI is on D10-D13; hardware PWM on D3/D5/D6/D9/D10/D11.

If a mic capsule is not in the library, use MAX9814_Module (capsule on board) instead of leaving MIC+/MIC- open.

Light-dependent resistor (photoresistor), GL5528: ~10-20 kOhm dark, ~1-10 kOhm lit
typicalApplication: A photoresistor is a RESISTANCE, not a voltage source: put it in a divider to read it. Rail -> LDR -> SENSE node -> fixed resistor (10 kOhm) -> GND, with SENSE on an ADC input; the voltage rises with light. Bright laser on the cell gives a low LDR resistance (high SENSE), a broken beam gives the opposite, so firmware compares SENSE against a CALIBRATED threshold with hysteresis rather than a hard-coded ADC value. Non-polarised, 2 leads on a 2.54 mm THT land.

companions.notes: Fixed divider resistor to GND; SENSE is the midpoint

description: 650 nm laser diode module, 3-5 V, ~40 mA, 3-pin (+ / - / TTL)
typicalApplication: External laser module on a 3-pin header: VCC to the 3.3-5 V rail, GND to GND, TTL (when present) to switch it. It draws ~30-40 mA, which is above an AVR/ESP32 GPIO's safe source current, so power it from the rail and switch it low-side (MMBT3904 + 1 kOhm base resistor) rather than powering it from a pin. In a beam-break alarm it points at the LDR; keep the beam path clear of tall parts and give both ends a mounting reference.

description: Single-digit 7-segment LED display, 0.56in, red, COMMON CATHODE, 10-pin THT (pins 3+8 = common cathode)

companions.notes: One series resistor PER SEGMENT (a-g + dp): 220-330 Ohm at 3.3-5 V for ~5-10 mA per segment. Never share one resistor across segments (brightness varies with the digit).

typicalApplication: COMMON CATHODE: tie BOTH COM pins (3 and 8) to GND; drive each segment a-g (+dp) from its own MCU GPIO through its own 220-330 Ohm resistor (segment lights when the GPIO is HIGH). Standard 10-pin pinout: 1=e 2=d 3=COM 4=c 5=dp 6=b 7=a 8=COM 9=f 10=g. Digit 0-9 = 7 GPIOs (+1 for dp); check total GPIO current (8 x 10 mA = 80 mA is fine for an ATmega/RP2040 in aggregate, but respect per-port limits) or use a 74HC595 shift register. Firmware: segment-pattern lookup table; a push-button counter debounces the switch and increments 0-9 with 9 -> 0 wrap.

description: Single-digit 7-segment LED display, 0.56in, red, COMMON ANODE, 10-pin THT (pins 3+8 = common anode)

companions.notes: One series resistor PER SEGMENT (a-g + dp): 220-330 Ohm at 3.3-5 V for ~5-10 mA per segment. Never share one resistor across segments (brightness varies with the digit).

typicalApplication: COMMON ANODE: tie BOTH COM pins (3 and 8) to the LED rail (3.3 V/5 V); each segment a-g (+dp) SINKS through its own 220-330 Ohm resistor into an MCU GPIO (segment lights when the GPIO is LOW - active-low patterns in firmware). Standard 10-pin pinout: 1=e 2=d 3=COM 4=c 5=dp 6=b 7=a 8=COM 9=f 10=g. Use 5161AS instead when you want active-high drive.

description: 4-digit 0.36in 7-segment LED display module with TM1637 driver, 2-wire (CLK/DIO), 3.3-5.5 V, 4-pin header
typicalApplication: Two GPIOs (CLK, DIO) + VCC + GND; the TM1637 does the segment scanning and current limiting so no per-segment resistors are needed. Good for counters, clocks and readouts up to 9999. Powering at 5 V with a 3.3 V MCU is fine (open-drain-style DIO with the module's pull-ups).

description: Capacitive touch sensor module (TTP223, 1 channel) with on-board touch pad, 2-5.5 V, active-high SIG output, 3-pin header (SIG/VCC/GND)
firmwareNotes: digitalRead(SIG): HIGH while touched (momentary mode by default; the A/B solder jumpers select toggle mode / active-low)
typicalApplication: Simplest touch switch: SIG -> any MCU GPIO (input), VCC -> 3.3 V or 5 V (SIG swings to VCC, so power it from the MCU's logic rail), GND -> GND. Toggle-on-touch is done in firmware (edge-detect SIG, debounce ~50 ms, flip the LED state). The module carries its own electrode; to make the PCB itself the button use TouchPad_D12mm on a touch-capable MCU pin instead.

description: Capacitive touch electrode: bare 12 mm round copper pad on the PCB (self-capacitance button under the soldermask), 1 pin
typicalApplication: Wire PAD to a touch-capable MCU input: ATtiny1614/ATtiny-series PTC channel (PA4-PA7/PB0-PB1 as X/Y lines), SAMD21 PTC pin, or an ESP32 TOUCHn pin (GPIO0/2/4/12-15/27/32/33). Keep other copper >= 1 mm away and NO ground pour under the pad; route the trace short and away from USB/power. Firmware: baseline at power-up, threshold with hysteresis, edge-detect + debounce, toggle the LED. If the MCU has no touch peripheral, use TTP223_Module.

description: MAX9814 electret microphone amplifier MODULE with AGC (Adafruit 1713-style breakout, mic capsule on board), 2.7-5.5 V, analog OUT (~1.25 V bias, 2 Vpp), 5-pin header GND/VDD/GAIN/OUT/AR
firmwareNotes: OUT sits at ~1.25 V DC with 2 Vpp audio: sample A0 fast, subtract the running mean, detect a short loud transient (peak > adaptive threshold) then lock out ~250 ms for one clap
typicalApplication: Clap/sound detector: OUT -> MCU ADC pin (safe on 3.3 V or 5 V ADCs), VDD -> 3.3-5 V, GND -> GND. GAIN: leave open = 60 dB, tie to VDD = 40 dB, tie to GND = 50 dB (50 dB is a good clap starting point). AR: leave open (1:500 attack/release), tie to VDD = 1:2000, GND = 1:4000. The AGC compresses steady sound, so detect the TRANSIENT (envelope rise) rather than a fixed level.

description: Sound sensor module (KY-038 / LM393 comparator + electret mic): analog AO and digital DO with on-board threshold pot, 3.3-5 V, 4-pin header AO/G/+/DO
firmwareNotes: DO goes HIGH on a sound above the pot threshold; count one clap per rising edge with a 200-300 ms lockout, or read AO for an adaptive detector
typicalApplication: Classic clap switch: DO -> MCU GPIO (rising-edge interrupt), or AO -> ADC for software detection; + -> 5 V (or 3.3 V), G -> GND. DO/AO swing to the + rail, so power the module from the MCU's logic rail (3.3 V for a 3.3 V MCU). Set the pot so speech does not trigger DO.

description: Analog water level sensor module (exposed parallel copper traces, ~40 mm sensing height), 3-5 V, output rises with immersion depth, 3-pin header S/+/-
firmwareNotes: Read S on an ADC; map calibrated dry/full readings to N levels with hysteresis; power the sensor from a GPIO only while sampling to slow electrode corrosion
typicalApplication: Tank level -> LED bar: S -> MCU ADC pin, + -> 3.3 V (or a GPIO switched on only during the reading), - -> GND; the analog value is split into levels in firmware and one LED per level (each through its own resistor) is lit progressively. Only 1 GPIO + 1 ADC needed - simpler than N bare probes. For discrete probes instead: one probe per level into MCU inputs with 100 kOhm pull-downs, a common probe on a GPIO driven HIGH only while sampling (avoids DC electrolysis), probes on screw terminals at the board edge.

description: Capacitive soil moisture sensor module v1.2 (TLC555 oscillator, corrosion-free probe), 3.3-5.5 V, analog AOUT (~1.5-3.0 V, LOWER when wet), 3-pin header AOUT/GND/VCC
firmwareNotes: AOUT is ~3.0 V in air and ~1.5 V in water at 5 V supply; calibrate DRY/WET, alert below a threshold with hysteresis (e.g. dry < 55 %, wet > 65 %) after averaging 10+ samples
typicalApplication: Plant/soil monitor: AOUT -> MCU ADC pin, VCC -> 3.3 V or 5 V, GND -> GND (a 3-wire MODULE - do NOT model a soil probe as a bare 2-pin header; a bare resistive probe needs a fixed resistor to GND to form a divider). Prefer this capacitive sensor over resistive probes: no DC through the soil, no electrode corrosion. Alert policy: short beep every few minutes while dry, not a continuous tone.

description: SPDT PCB power relay, 5 V coil (~72 mA, 70 Ohm), contacts 10 A @ 250 VAC / 30 VDC (Sanyou SRD Form C)

companions.notes: Low-side NPN switch: GPIO -> 1 kOhm -> base, COIL- to collector, emitter to GND. A relay coil draws ~72 mA - far over any GPIO.
Base resistor for the switching transistor.
MANDATORY flyback diode across the coil: cathode to COIL+ (the 5 V side), anode to COIL-. Without it the coil's collapse spike destroys the transistor.

typicalApplication: Switching a door lock / lamp / pump from an MCU. Coil side: 5 V rail -> COIL+, COIL- -> NPN collector (MMBT3904), emitter -> GND, GPIO -> 1 kOhm -> base, and a 1N4148WS flyback diode across the coil (cathode on COIL+). Contact side is fully isolated: bring COM plus NO (fail-secure: lock powered only while energised) or NC (fail-safe: lock releases on power loss) out to a screw terminal - state which you chose. Keep the contact traces wide and away from logic; a 12 V lock is powered from its own supply, not from the board's logic rail.

description: 1-channel 5 V opto-isolated relay module (on-board driver, flyback diode and screw terminals), active-LOW IN, 3-pin header IN/GND/VCC
firmwareNotes: Most of these boards are ACTIVE LOW: digitalWrite(pin, LOW) energises the relay. Verify on the module you buy.
typicalApplication: The no-fuss lock/appliance switch: IN -> any MCU GPIO, VCC -> 5 V, GND -> GND. The module already carries the transistor, the flyback diode, the opto-isolator and the COM/NO/NC screw terminals, so no discrete driver is needed on your PCB - which is why it is the right choice when the board only has to command the lock. Use the bare SRD-05VDC-SL-C instead when the relay must sit on your own PCB.
